chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Musa, from Zubyan ibn Hakim, from Musa ibn Ukeyl al-Numayri, from Maysara, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'It is from the weakening (of character) to neglect to reward (the guest), and from the roughness (of character) to make the guest serve (you). So when the guest lodges with you, aid him, and when he departs, do not aid him (in his departure), for it is from the lowness (of character). And provide for him, and make good his provision, for it is from the generosity.'
ai.seo_question: What is the proper etiquette for hosting a guest according to Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the 'weakness' of neglecting the guest and the 'roughness' of making them serve, establishing a balanced etiquette of hospitality. He instructs hosts to actively assist the guest during their stay but cease once they depart, while providing ample provisions to demonstrate true generosity (sakha'). This hadith underscores the spiritual merit of selfless service to visitors, a key virtue in Shia ethical tradition.
